value.headline: Early voting surge... / Early ballot totals cross 23 million...
value.claim: Democrats and unaffiliated voters are outpacing Republicans in turnout gains compared to 2022 in Kansas, Maine, Iowa and Nebraska; "Republicans are not as engaged."
value.evidence: KS: registered Democrats have cast 14.1% of their registration vs Republicans 6.7% (10/23) [M]; in 2022 at E-4 the shares were 21.2% vs 15.6% [M from R]. NE 2026 E-12 vs 2018 E-12: D share 41.9 vs 39.1, R 41.4 vs 48.5 [V]. It is a statement about the early pool, not the electorate: remaining expected pool is R+25 in KS and R+31 in NE by registration (pool.csv mid) [E].

rows.source: The Hill / IBTimes (quoting Michael McDonald): Early voting surge... / Early ballot totals cross 23 million...
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Midwest Early Vote Update Roundup ("signs of life for Republicans" per his Bluesky post)
value.claim: Early vote in Iowa, Kansas and Nebraska reveals signs of life for Republicans.
value.evidence: NE: Republicans took the cumulative early-vote lead on 10/23 (R 57,253 vs D 56,456) after D+9.9 on 10/7 [V UF]. KS: D margin among early voters D+27.2 (10/19) -> D+8.6 (10/23) [M]. The same drift happened in 2020: KS D+0.8 at E-11 -> R+10.0 final; NE R+1.6 -> R+7.5; OK D+11.2 -> R+4.8 [V EP].

rows.source: Michael McDonald (Substack, headline): Midwest Early Vote Update Roundup ("signs of life for Republicans" per his Blues
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Nebraska same-day comparison to 2022
value.claim: Nebraska early turnout is up vs 2022; registered Democrats' and unaffiliated turnout is up while Republican turnout is down.
value.cmp: same day 2022 (NE SOS file, not public)
value.evidence: The 2022 same-day NE file is not public; only his headline is visible (post paywalled). Against 2018 E-12 (NE SoS via ElectProject): Republican early ballots are UP 33% (39,223 -> 52,129) and Democrats up 67% (31,617 -> 52,829) [M]. So "Republican down" is at most a 2022-only statement.

rows.source: Michael McDonald (Bluesky): Nebraska same-day comparison to 2022
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: "... Democrats Lead Senate Polls in Key Trump Strongholds"
value.claim: Democrats lead Senate polls in key Trump strongholds (headline does not name states; tested here against KS and NE, the Trump-won states in this region with competitive Senate races).
value.evidence: KS: Hamilton +1.0 (8 polls, fake firm removed) but only +0.3 reweighted to 2024 recall [M]. NE: Osborn (independent, not a Democrat) trails by 0.7 (6 polls) and by 2.2 reweighted [M]. 2024 NE Senate polls were 4.8 pts too favourable to the same candidate, Osborn [M].
